concept.title: Search & filters
concept.shortdesc: Two boxes search, and they do different jobs. The one in the top bar searches every project you can see; the one above the list narrows the project you are in.

conbody.p: The top bar's box matches titles and bodies, and it also matches refs: type REQ-30 and REQ-30 comes back first, ahead of anything that merely mentions it. Case does not matter, so req-30 works, and a ref pasted out of a report with spaces around it still finds its artifact. Every result shows its ref beside the title, which is what tells two similarly named requirements apart. A longer ref that contains what you typed still appears below the exact match: REQ-3 finds REQ-3 first and leaves REQ-30 further down.

section.title: The search bar
section.p: Both boxes are search bars with chips. Each filter you add shows as a small coloured chip inside the bar, such as Status In review × or Owner Dave ×, so you can see at a glance what is narrowing the list. Click a chip's × to remove that filter alone. Whatever you type sits after the chips and searches as before; with the box empty, Backspace removes the last chip. Blue chips filter, purple chips group, and yellow chips are saved searches.
Typing suggests chips. Type dav and the bar offers Owner: Dave, Search Owner for: dav, Search Title for: dav and so on. Pick one with the arrow keys and Enter, or click it, and it becomes a chip.
The caret at the right of the bar opens a panel with three columns:

ul.li: Filters — the quick filters (Mine, In review, Failing, Suspect, each with how many it would show), then Status, Type, Priority, Created and Updated, each opening its values (for the dates: today, this week, this month, this quarter, this year). Ticking two values of one field shows either. Custom filter… builds a condition on any field or attribute: contains or is a value.

Group by — Status, Type, Priority, Owner or Heading, and Custom group for any attribute. The table then lists its rows under one heading per value; within a group, the rows keep their place in the hierarchy, and each group folds on its own. Two groupings combine ("Draft · Requirement"). Each grouping is a chip too.

Favourites — your saved searches. Save current search names the chips and text in the bar; tick Share with the workspace to list it for everyone in the workspace. Saved searches are kept with your account, so they follow you to every device. Choosing one puts it in the bar as a single chip; × beside one of your own deletes it.

section.p: Different filters all apply together: Status In review and Owner Dave shows Dave's artifacts in review. The arrow keys move through the panel and Escape closes it. On a phone the chips scroll sideways and the panel opens as a sheet from the bottom of the screen.
The chips are part of the page's address, so a filtered list can be bookmarked or shared: whoever opens the link sees the same chips, a saved search included.

section.title: The list's bar
section.p: The list's bar narrows the project you are in. Its text matches the ref, title, body, type and attributes. The type tabs beside it still narrow what the bar leaves, and count what each type holds.

section.title: The top bar's chips
section.p: In the top bar, the chips are Project, Type, Status and Owner (a part of a name or address is enough). Chips alone are a search: Type Test case with Owner dana lists Dana's test cases without any text. Typing a ref such as REQ-12 still finds it first, and Enter opens it. The results drop down below the bar, grouped by kind (Requirements, Test Cases, …), each with its project, owner and status. The chips it offers for what you typed come after the results.

A custom filter on Project, Type or Status matches their names: Status contains review finds the artifacts in review, and a name no status has finds nothing. The top bar's chips stay on one row that scrolls sideways, so the bar never grows over the page; hover a chip to read it in full.
